reason: The cited evidence supports the feasibility of creating a metastable solid solution via mechanical alloying (E1) and shows that a Mg-containing alloy can exhibit good corrosion resistance (E2), but it provides no direct support for the key mechanistic premises about intermetallic nucleation, growth, coarsening, or their specific effects on passivation and oxidation resistance.
premises: Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys can be produced in a metastable solid-solution state via non-equilibrium processing
Diffusion-controlled nucleation and growth of intermetallics occurs upon exposure to service temperatures
Fine, well-distributed intermetallics contribute to a stable, protective passivation layer that retains corrosion and oxidation resistance
Coarsening and clustering of intermetallics cause local depletion of alloying elements and impair the passivating film
The corrosion and oxidation performance of these alloys is directly linked to the morphology and distribution of intermetallic phases
